# @zakkster/lite-loglogn

Version: 0.6.0
License: MIT (c) Zahary Shinikchiev <shinikchiev@yahoo.com>
Runtime dependencies: none. ESM only. ASCII-only source. sideEffects: false.
Node: >= 18.

## What it is

A tree-shakeable, zero-GC family of sub-logarithmic bounded-integer
predecessor/successor data structures whose bound is proven by exact COUNTS. The
identity is the SPANNING framing: the family spans O(log_w U) to O(log log U)
over a bounded integer universe -- not a strict "O(log log U) only" package.
The FAMILY bound is O(log log U), in the universe size U (never the element
count n); StratifiedBitset itself is O(log_32 U), and XFastTrie is the first
strict O(log log U) member (queries only; its updates are O(w)); YFastTrie keeps
the O(log log U) query at O(n) space (updates: O(log log U) probes plus at most
2w-1 word moves, split / merge / borrow amortized); vEBTree (0.5.0) is
the worst-case member: O(log log U) for every operation, O(1) min / max, O(U) space;
RoaringSet (0.6.0) is the compressed member: 65,536-key chunks, each in the container kind
that fits its keys, over a universe up to 2^32, pools fixed at construction, a stated byte cost.
Every hot op of StratifiedBitset, XFastTrie, YFastTrie, vEBTree and RoaringSet allocates
zero bytes after construction (keys < 2^30; see the boxing note).

It is the O(log log U) sibling of @zakkster/lite-o1 (the constant) and
@zakkster/lite-logn (the logarithm in n): lite-loglogn holds the double
logarithm in U. StratifiedBitset does NOT claim a log2(w) line; "log2(w) must
win" belongs to the strict O(log log U) members (XFastTrie, YFastTrie and
vEBTree), proven there by counts.

Keys are w-bit integers in [0, U), U <= 2^32 (bitwise ops are 32-bit); wider keys
are a labeled SegmentedU variant, never a silent BigInt hot path. The SPACE price
is a co-headline on every member, stated with the same prominence as the time bound.

Roster (one member per release, append-only). StratifiedBitset (0.2.0),
XFastTrie (0.3.0), YFastTrie (0.4.0) and vEBTree (0.5.0) are published; RoaringSet
(0.6.0) is the fifth member:

- StratifiedBitset (0.2.0) -- array-embedded 32-ary bit pyramid. O(log_32 U)
  successor / predecessor; min / max read Lc words (Lc = levels <= 7);
  O(U/w) SPACE; 0 B/op on every hot method.
- XFastTrie (0.3.0) -- O(log log U) query via binary search over w pointer-free
  cuckoo LevelTables + a sorted leaf thread; O(w) UPDATE; O(n*w) SPACE,
  preallocated at a FIXED capacity.
- YFastTrie (0.4.0) -- the O(n)-space fix: an inner XFastTrie over O(n/w)
  representatives + bounded sorted Uint32Array buckets in one pool, no RNG.
  Queries O(log log U); updates O(log log U) probes + at most 2w-1 contiguous
  word moves (O(w)); split / merge / borrow AMORTIZED. O(n) SPACE, preallocated
  at a FIXED capacity.
- vEBTree (0.5.0) -- flattened van Emde Boas in ONE Uint32Array;
  worst-case O(log log U) has / add / delete / successor / predecessor, O(1)
  min / max; O(U) SPACE, the whole universe allocated up front; 0 B/op on every
  hot method (keys < 2^30).
- RoaringSet (0.6.0) -- Roaring-style compressed ordered set over [0, U), U <= 2^32:
  65,536-key chunks, each in the container kind that fits its keys (SINGLE / FULL 0 B,
  small array, array, bitmap with a summary, runs, small runs), preallocated pools
  that never grow, a direct or paged chunk table chosen at construction; successor /
  predecessor / min / max, addRange, cold counting set ops; SPACE fixed by the
  constructor arguments; 0 B/op on every hot method (keys < 2^30).

## Exports (from the single main file LogLogN.js)

- `VERSION` -- string. The package version; one of the three version sites
  (package.json / LogLogN.js VERSION const / this file's `Version:` header).
- `StratifiedBitset` -- class. An integer set over the fixed universe [0, U).
- `XFastTrie` -- class. An integer set over the fixed universe [0, U) with a
  fixed capacity; O(log log U) successor / predecessor, O(w) updates.
- `YFastTrie` -- class. Same method surface as XFastTrie; O(log log U)
  successor / predecessor in O(n) space.
- `vEBTree` -- class. An integer set over the fixed universe [0, U), U in
  [2, 2^32]; worst-case O(log log U) operations in O(U) space; no capacity, no seed.
- `RoaringSet` -- class. A compressed ordered integer set over the fixed universe
  [0, U), U in [1, 2^32]; positional pools (maxSmall, maxLarge, maxPages, pageBits)
  fixed at construction; byteLength is a closed form in the arguments. `dump()`
  returns a `RoaringSetDump` (types `RoaringSetDump` / `RoaringSetChunkDump`).

### StratifiedBitset

    import { StratifiedBitset } from '@zakkster/lite-loglogn';
    const s = new StratifiedBitset(1 << 20);
    s.add(5).add(70);                 // chainable, idempotent
    s.has(70);                        // true
    s.successor(5);                   // 70   (smallest key > 5)
    s.predecessor(70);                // 5    (largest key < 70)
    s.successor(70);                  // undefined (absent is undefined, never -1/null)
    for (let k = s.min(); k !== undefined; k = s.successor(k)) { /* walk */ }

Constructor: `new StratifiedBitset(universe)` -- universe an integer in
[1, 2^32] else RangeError `[lite-loglogn] universe must be an integer in
[1, 2^32]; got ...`. Fixed universe, no resize. Allocates one Uint32Array.

Getters (cold): `size`, `universe`, `levels` (= max(1, ceil(log2(U)/5)); 4 at
U = 2^16 and 2^20, 5 at 2^24, 6 at 2^28, 7 at 2^32), `byteLength` (4 x total
words of the one `_bits` Uint32Array).

Hot methods (0 B allocated):
- `has(x)` -> boolean
- `add(x)` -> this. Idempotent. Bad key -> RangeError `[lite-loglogn] key must be
  an integer in [0, U); got ...`, no state touched.
- `delete(x)` -> boolean (true if x was present)
- `successor(x)` -> number | undefined. STRICT: smallest key > x.
- `predecessor(x)` -> number | undefined. STRICT: largest key < x.
- `min()`, `max()` -> number | undefined (undefined when empty)

Cold: `clear()`; `dump()` -> { universe, size, words: Uint32Array[] } (ALLOCATES;
words[L] is a copy of level L, level 0 = key bits). No forEach, no iterator:
iterate with the successor walk.

Return conventions: absent = undefined (null is not zero, and not -1). -0 aliases
key 0. A bad key (not a number, non-integer, NaN, negative, >= U, null, string,
Symbol, BigInt, boxed Number) touches no word: has / delete -> false,
successor / predecessor -> undefined, add -> RangeError. For "at or after x" use
`s.has(x) ? x : s.successor(x)`.

Cost model (DETERMINISTIC; exact `_bits` word reads R / writes Wr, Lc = levels;
gated by test/Count.test.js through a counting Proxy over the shipped instance):
- has: R = 1
- add / delete when the key changes: R = Wr <= Lc (1 + the levels whose word
  changed emptiness); otherwise R = 1, Wr = 0
- successor / predecessor: R <= 2*Lc - 1 (a level-0 peel returns from the level-0
  word that holds x+1 / x-1 without touching level 1)
- min / max: R = Lc (R = 1 if empty)

Space (O(U/w); pinned in test/Space.test.js): U = 2^16 -> 8,460 B; 2^20 ->
135,300 B; 2^24 -> 2,164,804 B; 2^28 -> 34,636,836 B; 2^32 -> 554,189,332 B
(about 554 MB; the last two are formula values, never constructed in tests).

Boxing: hot methods allocate 0 bytes; a returned key >= 2^31 (>= 2^30 on a
pointer-compressed engine) may box as a HeapNumber when the call is not inlined.

### XFastTrie

    import { XFastTrie } from '@zakkster/lite-loglogn';
    const t = new XFastTrie(2 ** 32, 1024);   // universe, capacity (fixed)
    t.add(5).add(70);                         // chainable, idempotent
    t.successor(5);                           // 70   (STRICT, > 5)
    t.predecessor(70);                        // 5    (STRICT, < 70)
    t.successor(70);                          // undefined

Constructor: `new XFastTrie(universe, capacity, seed?)` -- universe an integer in
[2, 2^32], capacity an integer in [1, min(universe, 2^24)], else RangeError. The
optional seed is a uint32 integer: omitted / undefined / 0 = the default level
seeds bit for bit, else RangeError `[lite-loglogn] XFastTrie seed must be a uint32
integer in [0, 2^32-1]; got ...` (never random by default).
Allocates every column once; nothing is ever replaced except `_q` (nulled by a
poison, re-created by clear()). Getters (cold): `size`,
`universe`, `capacity`, `bits` (w = ceil(log2 U)), `byteLength`. Hot (0 B):
`has`, `add`, `delete`, `successor`, `predecessor`, `min`, `max` (same return
conventions as StratifiedBitset: absent = undefined, a bad key touches nothing,
-0 aliases 0, add of a bad key -> RangeError). Cold: `clear()` (restores the
constructed seeds -- the defaults, or those derived from the caller's seed --
and revives a poisoned instance), `dump()` -> { universe, capacity,
size, bits, keys: Uint32Array ascending, levels[L-1] = { capacity, prefix, min,
max } } (ALLOCATES).

Failure modes: add of a NEW key at size === capacity -> RangeError, no state
change. If 32 in-place reseed tries cannot place a key the add is rolled back
and throws RangeError; if the rollback itself fails the instance is POISONED:
every hot method throws TypeError on a valid key until clear().

Cost model (DETERMINISTIC; level-table TOUCHES counted through a Proxy over all
eight columns, test/XftCount.test.js; T = binary-search steps = log2(w) for
w = 2^j; m = shorter common prefix length of x with its thread neighbours):
- has: 1. successor / predecessor: 1 (x present), 1 + T (x absent). min / max: 0.
- add new key: 1 + T + (w - m). add present or full: 1.
- delete present: w - m. delete absent: 1. Any op with a bad key: 0.
- Rows are exact when no kick / reseed fires (add only).
- absent successor at w = 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 -> 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 touches; add into an
  empty trie (m = 0) -> 4, 7, 12, 21, 38 touches.

Caveats (stated plainly): FAST QUERY (1 + log2(w) touches when absent); O(w)
UPDATE (not O(log log U)); O(n*w) SPACE with FIXED capacity: byteLength =
13 TS + 12 (C+1) + 16 (w+1) + 16, TS = total level-table slots. Pinned
(DETERMINISTIC, test/XFastTrieSpace.test.js): (U, C) = (2^16, 1024) -> 225,580 B;
(2^20, 16384) -> 3,604,844 B; (2^32, 1) -> 3,896 B; (2^32, 65536) -> 31,457,836 B;
(2^32, 2^24) -> 4,563,403,308 B (worst case, formula only, about 4.6 GB). REPORTED
(node test/space-table.mjs, 2026-10-22, Node v26.8.2, deterministic bytes):
n = C = 1,000,000 at U = 2^20 -> 66,526,316 B vs StratifiedBitset 135,300 B
(491.7x); at U = 2^24 -> 175,578,284 B vs 2,164,804 B (81.1x); at U = 2^32 ->
393,682,220 B vs 554,189,332 B (0.71x). Dense universes favour StratifiedBitset;
XFastTrie pays off for a SPARSE set in a huge universe.
Hash-flood caveat: the cuckoo seeds are FIXED defaults, so adversarial keys can
force kick chains and reseeds (correctness holds, time suffers); see
decisions/0007-leveltable.md. Boxing: as StratifiedBitset (a returned key >= 2^31
may box when the call is not inlined).

### YFastTrie

    import { YFastTrie } from '@zakkster/lite-loglogn';
    const y = new YFastTrie(2 ** 32, 1000);   // universe, capacity (fixed), seed? (uint32)
    y.add(5).add(70);                         // chainable, idempotent
    y.successor(5);                           // 70   (STRICT, > 5)
    y.predecessor(70);                        // 5    (STRICT, < 70)
    y.successor(70);                          // undefined

Constructor: `new YFastTrie(universe, capacity, seed?)` -- universe an integer in
[2, 2^32], capacity an integer in [1, min(universe, 2^24)], else RangeError. Seed:
omitted / undefined / 0 = the default level seeds bit for bit (it is forwarded to
the inner XFastTrie), else a uint32 integer or RangeError `[lite-loglogn] YFastTrie
seed must be a uint32 integer in [0, 2^32-1]; got ...`. The seed never changes a
successful answer. Same getters (`size`, `universe`, `capacity`, `bits`,
`byteLength`) and hot methods (0 B: `has`, `add`, `delete`, `successor`,
`predecessor`, `min`, `max`) as XFastTrie, same return conventions. Cold: `clear()`
(restores the constructed state, caller's seed included; revives a poisoned
instance), `dump()` -> { universe, capacity, size, bits, keys: Uint32Array
ascending, reps: Uint32Array ascending (reps[0] = 0), sizes: Uint8Array } (ALLOCATES).

Policy (ADR 0008): w = ceil(log2 U), K = 2w, h = ceil(w/2). Reps are separators:
bucket i holds [rep_i, rep_{i+1}). The head rep 0 is permanent and holds 0..K keys;
every other bucket holds h..K. Split on a new key into a K-key bucket; merge into
the left neighbour (or borrow) when a non-head bucket of s <= h keys loses a key.
Deterministic: no RNG.

Claim (exact wording): queries are O(log log U); updates are O(log log U) probes
plus at most 2w-1 contiguous word moves (O(w)); a split / merge / borrow (at most
2w word moves plus an inner XFastTrie add, delete or both) is AMORTIZED. "O(log log
U) update" with no qualifier is not claimed.

Failure modes: add of a NEW key at size === capacity -> RangeError `YFastTrie is
full`, no state change. A split or borrow whose inner add stalls throws the inner
XFastTrie RangeError with the set UNCHANGED, so `add` AND `delete` (a delete may
borrow) can throw on a valid key. If the inner rollback fails the instance is
POISONED: every hot method throws TypeError on a valid key (min / max always) until
clear(). Bad keys behave as in XFastTrie.

Cost model (DETERMINISTIC; test/YftCount.test.js, a Proxy over `_bk`, `_bn` and the
eight inner columns; lambda = 1 if x is a rep else 1 + T, T = log2(w); beta = binary
search reads over a bucket of s keys; lb = lower-bound index; rows are WHOLE ops,
the split row replaces the plain add row, merge / borrow replace the plain delete
row; m, m' = early stops of the inner add / delete):
- has / add present / add full / delete absent: lambda touches, beta + [lb < s] reads, 0 moves.
- successor / predecessor: lambda, beta + <= 2 (+ hop), 0. min / max: 0, <= 1 (+ hop), 0.
- add new, no split: lambda, beta + [lb < s], s - lb moves + 1 write.
- delete present, no merge / borrow: lambda, beta + 1, s - lb - 1 moves.
- add new, split (s = K): lambda + 1 + T + (w - m), beta + [lb < s] + 1, w + (w - lb') + 1 write (<= 2w).
- delete present, merge: lambda + (w - m), beta + 1, s - 1 moves.
- delete present, borrow: lambda + 1 + T + (w - m) + (w - m'), beta + 2, floor(t/2) <= 2w moves (t = s_L + s - 1).
- Gated: an absent successor from a bucket of s = 2w-1 keys costs touches + probes =
  4, 6, 8, 10, 12 at w = 2, 4, 8, 16, 32; a plain update moves <= 2w-1 words; a split /
  merge / borrow <= 2w; an inner reseed <= 32 tries.

SPACE (O(n), preallocated at the capacity; formula pinned from a test-owned model,
test/YFastTrieSpace.test.js): byteLength = 4 (Cr+1) K + (Cr+1) + 16 + the inner
XFastTrie(U, Cr).byteLength, Cr = min(2 + floor(C/h), U), K = 2w. REPORTED (node
test/space-table.mjs, 2026-10-25, Node v26.8.2, deterministic bytes): n = C =
1,000,000 at U = 2^20 -> 27,524,503 B (XFastTrie 66,526,316 B, ratio 0.414; 203.4x
StratifiedBitset); at U = 2^24 -> 34,123,672 B (0.194 of XFastTrie); at U = 2^32 ->
47,484,715 B (0.121 of XFastTrie, 0.086 of StratifiedBitset); n = C = 1,000 at
U = 2^32 -> 64,637 B (0.099). Smaller than XFastTrie in every cell of that table
(0.099 .. 0.529); a dense universe still favours StratifiedBitset.

Boxing: hot methods allocate 0 bytes for keys < 2^30; a returned key >= 2^31 (>= 2^30
on a pointer-compressed engine), or a rep that large passed to the inner add / delete
of a split / merge / borrow, may box a HeapNumber when the call is not inlined.

### vEBTree

    import { vEBTree } from '@zakkster/lite-loglogn';
    const v = new vEBTree(2 ** 16);           // universe [0, 2^16); allocated up front
    v.add(5).add(70);                         // chainable, idempotent
    v.successor(5);                           // 70   (STRICT, > 5)
    v.predecessor(70);                        // 5    (STRICT, < 70)
    v.successor(70);                          // undefined
    v.min(); v.max();                         // 5 70
    v.byteLength;                             // 8232

Constructor: `new vEBTree(universe)` -- universe an integer in [2, 2^32], else
RangeError `[lite-loglogn] vEBTree universe must be an integer in [2, 2^32]; got ...`.
No capacity, no seed, no resize. Methods: `has(x)` -> boolean, `add(x)` -> this
(idempotent), `delete(x)` -> boolean, `successor(x)` / `predecessor(x)` -> number |
undefined (STRICT), `min()` / `max()` -> number | undefined (O(1)), `clear()` ->
void (cold; rewrites the constructed layout in place). Getters (cold, read-only):
`size`, `universe`, `bits` (w = ceil(log2 U)), `byteLength` (4 x the words of the one
`_t` Uint32Array). No `dump()`, no `forEach`, no iterator: iterate with the
`successor` walk. A bad key (not a number, non-integer, NaN, negative, >= U, null,
string, Symbol, BigInt, boxed Number) touches nothing: has / delete -> false,
successor / predecessor -> undefined, add -> RangeError `[lite-loglogn] key must be
an integer in [0, U); got ...`. `-0` aliases key 0. A returned key >= 2^31 (>= 2^30
on a pointer-compressed engine) may box a HeapNumber when the call is not inlined.
Allocation: hot methods 0 B (keys < 2^30; torture V1-V5, below); clear() 0 B (cold,
`_t.fill(0)` + header rewrite, no new buffer); the constructor allocates `_t`, `_g`,
`_p` once. On V8 14.6 (Node v26.8.2) successor / predecessor are never inlined
(traced 2026-11-03 in Maglev and TurboFan, default flags, untimed: bytecode 850 / 838 B
exceeds the 460 B inlining limit), so a returned key >= 2^31 boxes: 16 B per call (measured, torture
control CV7). Scoped to that V8; other engines / versions are not claimed.

Bound: worst-case O(log log U) for has / add / delete / successor / predecessor and
O(1) for min / max; no hashing, no reseed, no amortized step. Depth is
ceil(log2(w / 8)) internal levels (0 for w <= 8, 1 for w = 9 .. 16, 2 for w = 17 .. 32).

Layout (decisions/0009-veb-flattening.md): ONE Uint32Array. A node of width w <= 8 is
a LEAF, a plain bitmap (no header, no summary). A node of width w >= 9 is INTERNAL:
lo = (w > 24 ? 16 : 8), hi = w - lo; a [min, max] header (EMPTY = min > max, stored
[0xFFFFFFFF, 0]; header keys node-relative, only the root's are full 32-bit keys), then
the summary (width hi), then 2^hi clusters of width lo. min is NOT stored in its
cluster, so an add or a delete follows one path. S(w) = 2 + S(hi) + 2^hi S(lo) words.
Only the ROOT's cluster count is trimmed, to ceil(U / 2^lo).

SPACE (O(U), the whole universe allocated by the constructor; exact byteLength,
formula and engine agree, pinned in test/VEBTree.test.js):

| U | w | byteLength |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 1 | 4 B |
| 257 | 9 | 76 B |
| 2^16 | 16 | 8,232 B |
| 2^20 | 20 | 131,604 B |
| 2^24 | 24 | 2,105,392 B |
| 2^24 + 1 | 25 | 2,115,708 B (trimmed root) |
| 2^28 | 28 | 33,718,804 B |
| 2^32 | 32 | 539,500,592 B |

That is about 0.97 of StratifiedBitset's bytes for w = 13 .. 32 (0.985 at w = 12, 1.000 at
w = 11), and a little more below that (1.118 at U = 2^9, 1.061 at U = 2^10): vEBTree is not a space win. For a sparse
key set in a large universe use YFastTrie (O(n) space).

Expected loss row vs StratifiedBitset (ADR 0009; verdicts by words read, gated EXACTLY
in test/VebCount.test.js, never written as counts in prose): WIN min / max (test
'A3 exact rows, all 3 columns == vebCost, ...' and 'A3 StratifiedBitset side via the
Count.test.js harness, ...'); WIN (expected; only the vEB side is gated, 'A3 exact rows ...') out-of-range successor / predecessor, answered from a header; at U = 2^16 LOSE far-gap successor, LOSE same-word successor
and LOSE has ('A3 vEB vs SB loss row, U=2^16 (...)'; the title carries the gated
counts). The member is for the worst case: no restructuring tail. Timing is REPORTED only
(VEB-WITNESS block above): StratifiedBitset reads fewer words outside min / max and
header-decided successor / predecessor; vEBTree is the textbook O(log log U) member.

### RoaringSet

    import { RoaringSet } from '@zakkster/lite-loglogn';
    const s = new RoaringSet(2 ** 32);            // universe [0, 2^32); default pools, direct table
    s.paged;                                      // false
    s.add(5).add(70);                             // chainable, idempotent
    s.addRange(1000000, 2000000);                 // keys 1000000 .. 1999999
    s.successor(5);                               // 70   (STRICT, > 5)
    s.predecessor(70);                            // 5    (STRICT, < 70)
    s.min(); s.max();                             // 5 1999999
    s.byteLength;                                 // 3036180

Constructor: `new RoaringSet(universe, maxSmall = 1024, maxLarge = 256, maxPages = all,
pageBits = 8)`, positional. universe REQUIRED, an integer in [1, 2^32], else RangeError
`[lite-loglogn] RoaringSet universe must be an integer in [1, 2^32]; got ...`.
maxSmall [0, 65535], maxLarge [1, 65534], pageBits [1, 15], maxPages [1, ceil(C /
2^pageBits)] (C = ceil(U / 65536)); a bad knob is RangeError `[lite-loglogn] RoaringSet
<knob> must be an integer in [lo, hi]; got ...` (maxPages: `... maxPages must be an
integer in [1, N] for this universe and pageBits; got ...`). Every pool is preallocated
once and never grows. Methods: `has(x)` -> boolean, `add(x)` -> this (idempotent),
`addRange(lo, hi)` -> this (keys [lo, hi), 0 <= lo <= hi <= U; prechecks, throws before
any write; a bad bound is RangeError; each touched chunk ends in the kind runOptimize would
pick, except that the first partial chunk can end as a large-slot array (fewer keys than twice its runs) where
small runs would fit, which runOptimize keeps), `delete(x)` -> boolean, `successor(x)` /
`predecessor(x)` -> number | undefined (STRICT), `min()` / `max()` -> number |
undefined, `runOptimize()` -> this (cold; idempotent, a second call changes no chunk; add never
re-encodes, call it after clustered ingestion), `intersects(other)` -> boolean and `intersectionSize(other)` /
`unionSize(other)` / `differenceSize(other)` -> number (cold counting ops, nothing
materialized; other must be a RoaringSet of the same universe, any layout / pageBits,
else TypeError / RangeError), `clear()` -> void (cold), `dump()` -> RoaringSetDump
{ universe, size, paged, chunks: [{ chunk, kind, count, runs }] } (cold, allocating;
kind in single | small | array | bitmap | runs | smallRuns | full). Getters (cold,
read-only): `size`, `universe`, `paged`, `byteLength`. No forEach, no iterator, no
rank / select: iterate with the successor walk. A bad key (not a number, non-integer,
NaN, negative, >= U, null, string, Symbol, BigInt, boxed Number) touches nothing: has /
delete -> false, successor / predecessor -> undefined, add -> RangeError `[lite-loglogn]
key must be an integer in [0, U); got ...`. `-0` aliases key 0. A returned key >= 2^31
(>= 2^30 on a pointer-compressed engine) may box a HeapNumber when the call is not
inlined. addRange: Allocates nothing for bounds < 2^30; a bound >= 2^31 boxes at a non-inlined call site (as has).

Failure modes (all throw BEFORE any write, set unchanged): container pool exhaustion,
`[lite-loglogn] RoaringSet small/large container pool exhausted (capacity N); increase
pool capacity at construction` (pool name small/large or large); page pool exhaustion
(paged layout only), `[lite-loglogn] RoaringSet metadata page pool exhausted (maxPages
N); increase maxPages at construction`. So add AND delete can throw on a valid key: a
delete from a FULL chunk needs a slot, and a delete splitting a small-runs run past 32
runs needs a large slot. addRange throws when the pools cannot hold the slots / pages it
needs (its page-pool text: `[lite-loglogn] RoaringSet addRange metadata page pool exhausted
(needs N new page(s), F free of maxPages M); increase maxPages at construction`; a slot
shortfall throws the add() container-pool text). The precount follows
the write order and counts only each chunk's final container, so under pool pressure addRange can
succeed where the equivalent add loop would throw part-way, and a range can throw where its final
state would fit.

Layout: each 65,536-key chunk is held in the container kind that fits its keys (SINGLE and
FULL cost 0 B; small array 2..64 keys; array up to 4,096; bitmap; runs; small runs <=
32 runs), with promote / demote hysteresis. The chunk table is DIRECT (11 B per chunk)
or PAGED (a directory plus pooled 2^pageBits-row pages, page 0 a shared zero page),
chosen once at construction: paged iff 11 (maxPages + 1) 2^pageBits + 2 ceil(C /
2^pageBits) + 4 maxPages + 2 < 11 C (strict). The default constructor is direct at every U.

SPACE (fixed by the constructor arguments; exact byteLength, formula and engine agree,
pinned in test/DocSync.test.js): direct = 8,460 + 11 C + 130 maxSmall + 8,456
(maxLarge + 1) + 2 maxLarge; paged replaces 11 C by 11 (maxPages + 1) 2^pageBits +
2 ceil(C / 2^pageBits) + 4 maxPages + 2.

| U | (maxSmall, maxLarge, maxPages, pageBits) | layout | byteLength |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2^16 | defaults (1024, 256, all, 8) | direct | 2,315,295 B |
| 2^25 | (0, 1, 1, 8) | direct | 31,006 B |
| 2^26 | (0, 1, 1, 8) | paged | 31,020 B |
| 184,942,592 | (0, 1, 10, 8) | direct (tie, strict <) | 56,416 B |
| 2^32 | defaults (1024, 256, all, 8) | direct | 3,036,180 B |
| 2^32 | (0, 1, all, 8) | direct | 746,270 B |
| 2^32 | (0, 1, 1, 8) | paged | 31,524 B |
| 2^32 | (0, 1, 254, 8) | paged | 744,984 B |
| 2^32 | (0, 1, 255, 8) | direct (722,430 is not < 720,896) | 746,270 B |
| 2^32 | (0, 1, 1000, 6) | paged | 736,128 B |

The empty floor is a pool-sizing choice: at U = 2^32 the default pools alone are 2,306,824 B
(DETERMINISTIC: the 2^32 default row minus 8,460 minus the direct table 11 C = 720,896).

Timing for RoaringSet is REPORTED only: the one witness:roar run is under "Gates and
measurements" below (REPORTED, gates nothing).

  (R^2 0.6589); no R^2 floor or slope band is gated. lite-o1 BitSet is faster where
  it applies (4.28-4.82 vs 4.87-7.61 ns/op at n = 4096, w = 16..24).

## Design bounds

- Zero runtime deps; node:test only; ASCII-only source.
- Single PascalCase main file LogLogN.js; sideEffects: false; tree-shakeable
  named exports, no barrel.
- Bounded integer universe, word-RAM model: keys are w-bit integers in [0, U),
  w <= 32. Fixed, preallocated capacity. Fail closed on every unverified state;
  `null` is not zero; an out-of-universe key fails closed.
- typeof-guard FIRST, before any coercion, at the door of every op (the recurring
  Symbol / BigInt / {valueOf} / boxed-Number footgun).
- Zero allocation on every steady-state hot path of StratifiedBitset, XFastTrie,
  YFastTrie and vEBTree (0 B/op; keys < 2^30), proven by `node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs`.
- SPACE is a co-headline: every member states its footprint bound alongside its
  time bound.

## Cross-package boundaries

- @zakkster/lite-o1 -- the O(1) sibling. Any BOUNDED-INTEGER priority queue is
  O(1) and belongs there (Dial's bucket queue). Its BitSet: for U <= 2^25 and
  successor-only use lite-o1 BitSet (fixed 3 levels, O(1) in U); StratifiedBitset
  owns predecessor / max, U up to 2^32, labelled O(log_32 U), and returns undefined
  for absent (lite-o1 BitSet returns -1).
- @zakkster/lite-logn -- the O(log n) sibling. A general comparator ordered map is
  O(log n) and belongs there.
- @zakkster/lite-filter -- owns approximate / probabilistic membership;
  lite-loglogn owns exact ordered integer structures. No overlap; no use of it.
- @zakkster/lite-fastbit32 -- owns the clz32 / word-bit primitives; lite-loglogn
  cross-links its recipe, never a drifting reimplementation (decision D-05).
